official_sources.title: Title Number and UPRN Look Up technical specification

verified_claims: The National Polygon Dataset publishes HMLR index polygons for England and Wales.
A registered title normally has a title plan, register and one or more index polygons.
Title plans and registers record the general position of boundaries unless an exact boundary has been determined.
Index polygons show indicative title location and must not be treated as exact legal extents.
Every registered title has at least one index polygon.
Poly_ID identifies the polygon while Title_No links polygons to registered titles and related datasets.
INSERT, UPDATE, Vers_No and Rec_Status provide lifecycle information.
Rec_Status values distinguish added, changed and deleted records.
Index polygon geometry must be a single area.
Index polygons can be the same size, larger or smaller than the title-plan extent.
Small gaps, overlaps, slivers and underlaps exist and may be genuine or technical inconsistencies.
Technical polygon overlaps do not necessarily indicate a real title conflict.
Ownership boundaries do not always follow features mapped in OS MasterMap.
All HMLR index polygons are captured in British National Grid.
National Polygon, Title Descriptor and UPRN datasets are separated but link through title number.
Title Descriptor gives estate interest, class of title and registered status.
A title number can have only one class of title in Title Descriptor.
Title–UPRN links exist only where HMLR can establish an address relationship with AddressBase.
A title may have multiple UPRNs and a title can have no UPRN even when an external UPRN exists.
National Polygon Service full, change-only and validation releases are monthly and licensed/chargeable.
